name: Jersey
summary: Jersey is not in the EU or EEA and, since Brexit, EU citizens have no free movement there: they are treated like other foreign nationals. British and Irish citizens can live in Jersey under the Common Travel Area, but still need a housing and work status. For everyone else the main routes are an employer-sponsored work permit (with a visa where required) and, for the wealthy, discretionary Entitled status as a High Net Worth Individual, indicated by taxable income above GBP 1.25 million a year. The old GBP 2 million investor route is closed.
naturalisation: British citizenship through the Jersey Customs and Immigration Service: generally 5 years' residence in the UK or the Islands with indefinite leave or settled status, with at least 12 months after indefinite leave; English language and Life in the UK test (including a Jersey supplement). Fee GBP 1,709 for naturalisation.
dual_citizenship_note: Not verified from a source in this research.

routes.limited_places: Discretionary: the Housing and Work Control Panel recommends status on economic or social grounds; meeting the indicators does not guarantee approval. Locate Jersey says there is no cap on grants.
routes.processing_time: Locate Jersey reportedly quotes 15 working days from a complete application (law-firm report, not confirmed on an official page)
routes.family: Locate Jersey asks for passport copies for each person relocating; terms for family members not researched.
routes.tax_note: Under the old HVR regime holders pay 20% on the first GBP 1,250,000 of worldwide income and 1% above it (Jersey property income at 20%). Whether this tax regime continues unchanged after the 2026 reform was not confirmed.
routes.name: High Value Residency: Entitled status for High Net Worth Individuals (formerly 2(1)(e))
routes.summary: Wealthy, economically active people can be granted Entitled status, which gives full access to Jersey's housing and job markets. It is a discretionary grant for people who bring economic or social benefit, not a purchase of residence, and UK-style immigration clearance is also needed.
routes.requirements: Control of Housing and Work (Residential and Employment Status) Regulations, Regulation 5 (in force from mid-September 2026, replacing Article 2(1)(e) and the Housing and Work Advisory Group): the Housing and Work Control Panel must recommend Entitled status as justified on economic or social grounds and in the community's best interests; due diligence and KYC. Law-firm commentary says the policy indicators are taxable income above GBP 1.25 million a year for at least 10 years and/or philanthropic or community contributions of at least GBP 100,000 a year, and that these are not in the legislation. Locate Jersey's criteria page (not clearly updated for the 2026 change) still lists: ability to generate a minimum tax contribution of GBP 250,000 a year, worldwide income above GBP 1,250,000, and personal wealth above GBP 10 million excluding the main residence. Expected to buy or rent a home of typically GBP 3.5 million or more (house) or GBP 1.75 million or more (apartment); buy after 12 months of renting. Approved applicants also need UK immigration clearance. Status can be withdrawn if conditions stop being met.
routes.physical_presence: Must make Jersey the main home; no published day count found

routes.status_note: Closed to new applicants; paragraph 224A of the Jersey Immigration Rules refers to leave that pre-dates 12 April 2022. Only existing holders can extend or settle.
routes.name: Investor route (GBP 2 million) under the Jersey Immigration Rules
routes.summary: A route for people investing GBP 2 million in Jersey on terms set by the Minister. It no longer accepts new applicants.
routes.requirements: Jersey Immigration Rules paras 224-231: age 18 or over; GBP 2 million of own money disposable in Jersey, invested on terms the Minister judges beneficial to Jersey; Jersey as main home; no recourse to public funds; entry clearance. Indefinite leave after 5 continuous years plus English and life-in-Jersey knowledge.
routes.physical_presence: Main home in Jersey; absences of 180 days or less in each 12 months for indefinite leave

routes.limited_places: Needs Ministerial approval and any licence required under the Control of Housing and Work Law; discretionary
routes.name: Person establishing himself in business (entry clearance route)
routes.summary: The Jersey Immigration Rules still contain a route for someone to take over, join or set up a business in Jersey, with 2 years' initial leave and settlement after 5 years. Ministerial approval is needed and no capital figure is published in the rules.
routes.requirements: Jersey Immigration Rules paras 200-210: Ministerial approval; any licence needed under the Control of Housing and Work (Jersey) Law 2012; entry clearance. Initial leave up to 2 years without freedom to take other employment, extensions up to 3 years at a time, indefinite leave after 5 continuous years if still in the business, with audited accounts and English and life-in-Jersey knowledge. Whether it is open in practice was not confirmed on a government page.
routes.physical_presence: Continuous residence; absences of 180 days or less in each 12 months for indefinite leave

routes.limited_places: Employer must hold the right Housing and Work permission and the job must be on the eligible list; permit tied to named employer and role
routes.fees_note: Employer fee for a permit of more than 2 and up to 3 years (GBP 290 for 1 to 2 years). Further leave fee GBP 943. Visa fees not sourced.
routes.processing_time: About 3 weeks for a complete application (government page)
routes.family: Dependants allowed if the permit is for more than 12 months.
routes.name: Long-term work permit (employer-sponsored)
routes.summary: An employer applies for a work permit for a named person in an eligible job. Up to 3 years at a time; time counts toward settlement and dependants are allowed.
routes.requirements: Immigration (Work Permits) (Jersey) Rules 1995 and the Work Permit Policy: job at RQF level 3 or above (unless an exception applies), salary at or above the occupation threshold or the going rate (examples: chief executive GBP 84,100, construction manager GBP 50,100), English B1 or higher, contract, adequate accommodation, age 18 or over. Many employees also need a UK-administered visa. The employer must hold a Control of Housing and Work permission before applying. Short and annual temporary permits (agriculture, hospitality, construction, fishing) do not count toward settlement.
routes.physical_presence: Live and work in Jersey for the named employer; absences of 180 days or less in each 12 months for settlement

routes.name: Common Travel Area: British and Irish citizens
routes.summary: British and Irish citizens need no visa or work permit to enter and work in Jersey. They still need a Control of Housing and Work status, which starts as Standard and gives full rights after 10 years (Entitled) or 5 years (Entitled for Work Only).
routes.requirements: Jersey is part of the Common Travel Area with the UK, Ireland, Guernsey and the Isle of Man (Jersey Immigration Rules para 15; Irish citizens, paras 5-5B). Under the Control of Housing and Work Law a person who expects to be ordinarily resident must apply for a registration card within 3 months and cannot work without one. Entitled status after 10 years' ordinary residence without break; Entitled for Work Only after 5.
routes.physical_presence: Ordinary residence; breaks reset the Entitled qualifying periods

open_questions: The Housing and Work Control Panel regime (Regulation 5) took effect in mid-September 2026; the exact commencement date and the text of the Regulations were not read. The GBP 1.25 million / GBP 100,000 indicators come from law-firm commentary, and Locate Jersey's older page still shows GBP 250,000 minimum tax, GBP 10 million wealth and the property minimums.
Whether the 20%/1% HVR tax regime and the property purchase minimums still apply after the 2026 reform is not confirmed.
Fees for HVR applications and for the UK-administered visa were not found; government fees left null for HVR.

Exact immigration permission HVR holders receive (visa type, route to indefinite leave) not found; path_to_permanent_years of 0 reflects that Entitled status is itself the housing/work right, not immigration settlement.
Whether the business-person route (paras 200-210) is open to new applicants in practice and what capital is expected was not confirmed.
Dual citizenship under British naturalisation was not verified from an official source.
Whether EU citizens face any special visa treatment in Jersey after the end of the EU Settlement Scheme not confirmed beyond the gov.je visa page.
Salary thresholds and the eligible occupation list for long-term work permits only partly read (page truncated).
Fee page and Jersey Rules were read from gov.je without an effective date for the fees.
